## 1. Executive Summary | Goal | Approach | KPI Benchmarks | |------|----------|----------------| | **Localised price‑point** that respects purchasing power, payment habits and family‑sharing norms while preserving a defensible unit‑economic profile for investors | • Tiered, currency‑native pricing plus flexible payment rails (mobile‑money, QR‑code, installments, BNPL)
• “Ad‑supported Basic” and “Premium + Family‑bundle” options that match regional consumption patterns
• Dynamic pricing & promotional engines that keep ARPU and churn in line with the global target | • ARPU (USD) ≥ $5.75
• CAC pay‑back < 5 months
• LTV / CAC ≥ 3 • Gross margin ≥ 70% (after conversion costs) | --- ## 2. Market‑Level Context | Region | Median MRR (USD) | Preferred payment rails | Family‑sharing culture | Attitude to Recurring Billing | |--------|-----------------|--------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------| | **Africa** | $1–$4 | Mobile‑money (M‑Pesa, MTN‑MoMo), QR, small‑installments (< 3 months) | **Very** high – “one‑subscription for household” common; 3‑5 people share 1 seat | Reluctant to long‑term contracts; prefer short‑term or “pay‑as‑you‑go” plans | | **South Asia** | $2–$6 | UPI, GCash, Paytm, mobile‑money, 12‑month BNPL | High – “family sharing” and “social sharing” are norm; 4‑6 seats common | Mixed; urban audiences increasingly comfortable with monthly billing | | **Latin America** | $3–$8 | QR, credit‑cards (installments up to 12 months), bank‑transfer, UPI‑style | High – “several family members” share a plan; “Household‑Bundle” popular | Mid‑to‑high acceptance of monthly billing, but high sensitivity to inflation and currency risk | **Implication:** - Pricing must be *country‑specific* but *consistent in value perception* across the board. - Payment options should mirror local habits; the “monthly” name can be re‑branded (e.g., “One‑Month‑Pay” or “Monthly Installment”) to fit cultural norms. - Family sharing must be built into the subscription logic, not forced upon users. --- ## 3. Pricing Architecture (Core Framework) | Tier | Global Feature Set | Sub‑Region Adaptations | Suggested Local Price (per month) | Notes | |------|--------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------| | **Basic‑Ad** | 480 p‑b‑p, mobile‑only, 1 device | • Free in low‑income markets (Africa, rural SEA)
• Limited ad volume in Latin America | 0 USD (Africa), 0 USD (rural SEA), $0.95 USD (LatAm) | Revenue share from ads → helps subsidise lower‑price tiers | | **Standard** | HD, 3 devices, ad‑free | • Monthly payment via mobile‑money / QR
• 4‑month / 12‑month installment bundles | $3.75 USD (Africa), $5.25 USD (South Asia), $7.00 USD (LatAm) | Standard 1‑month = 1 local‑currency *USD conversion* | | **Premium** | Ultra‑HD, 5 devices, ad‑free, early‑access | • 12‑month annual plan | $5.75 USD (Africa), $7.50 USD (South Asia), $10.00 USD (LatAm) | Upsell to families via discounted “Household‑Bundle” | | **Premium‑Family** | 8 devices, 2‑hour simultaneous streams, family‑badge perks | • 5‑person “household” plan, 1‑month trial | $9.00 USD (Africa), $11.50 USD (South Asia), $15.00 USD (LatAm) | 15% discount over 5 × Premium price | ### Currency Handling * All prices are stored in **local currency** (NGN, INR, MXN, etc.) but displayed in users’ home currency. * **Price conversion** happens on sign‑up: local price → USD (for reporting) using live FX rates + a 1% margin to cover conversion costs. * To keep unit economics defensible, we maintain a **Target ARPU‑USD** of **$5.75** and adjust local rates so that the weighted average converges on that figure after accounting for currency volatility. --- ## 4. Flexible Payment & Installment Engine | Payment Rail | How It Feeds Subscriptions | Revenue Capture | Cash‑Flow Mitigation | |--------------|---------------------------|----------------|---------------------| | **Mobile‑Money / QR** | User sends OTP / scans QR → instant transaction → subscription activated | 100 % in‑hour capture | No delay; minimal risk | | **Full‑Month** | Direct debit or one‑time charge | Immediate | Straight‑through | | **Installments (≤ 12 months)** | Payment plan split into X equal credit‑card / BNPL payments | 100 % captured over 12 months | We accrue *Deferred Revenue* until each installment is paid. To stay conservative, we apply a **30‑day cash‑flow hedge** and treat unearned revenue as a **liability** (standard IFRS 15). | | **Pay‑Later / BNPL** | User chooses “Pay Later” → lender funds upfront | Immediate cash inflow for company | Mitigates perceived risk of long‑term contracts in low‑income markets. | | **Short‑Term “Pay‑As‑You‑Go”** | 15‑day prepaid passes (value = 25 % of Monthly) | Cash inflow within 15 days | Ideal for markets with high non‑recurring billing acceptance. | **Implementation note:** Set a **maximum install‑ment‑period of 12 months** in Africa and South Asia (due to higher credit risk), but allow 24‑month plans in Latin America where banking penetration is higher. --- ## 5. Family‑Sharing Rules – The “Household‑Bundle” Logic | Rule | Regional Variation | Incentive | |------|------------------|-----------| | **Seating limit** | 5 seats in Africa, 8 in South Asia, 10 in Latin America | More seats align with higher household size in Latin America | | **Name‑based seats** | 1 primary + 4 “secondary” seats (no login required) | Enables effortless sharing | | **Revenue split** | 30 % goes to household member’s “Family‑Share” account | Encourages cross‑promotions via in‑app referrals | | **Subscription length** | Family plan is only 6‑month/annual, not monthly | Encourages early commitment in high‑churn markets | | **Promotional credit** | 1‑month free for a relative who never had a subscription | Reduces entry barrier | **Outcome:** - 70 % of “Base‑Currency” revenue stays with the head‑subscriber but is automatically allocated **$X** to each family seat. - In African markets, the *effective price* per seat is ~ $1.5–$2.0, still above the median per‑capita discretionary spend. - In South Asia/Latin America, price per seat rises to ~$3–$4, matching household spending on premium services. --- ## 6. Ad‑Supported Revenue Layer | Segment | Ad Tier | Pricing | Revenue Share | |---------|---------|---------|----------------| | **Free/Ad‑Basic** | 3–4 ads / episode | 0 USD | 60 % to platform; 40 % to creators | | **Ad‑Free (Standard/Premium)** | 0 ads | Paid | 100 % to platform | ### Ad‑Supported **ARPU** Impact - In countries with low willingness to pay (e.g., rural Africa), **Free + In‑app “ad‑plus‑premium” bundle** can capture ~ 55% of potential users, generating ~ $0.4 USD per user/month. - Combined with Tiered subscriptions, the **overall weighted ARPU** climbs to the target $5.75 USD once the *High‑Value* Premium families are included. --- ## 7. Consolidated Revenue Reporting – How We Keep Unit Economics Strong 1. **Currency Conversion** * All local‑currency transactions are converted to USD for consolidated reporting using the **mid‑market rate** of the **settlement day**. * A small **currency risk margin (1–2 %)** is added to counter FX volatility and to reflect hedging costs (if needed). 2. **Deferred Revenue Accounting** * Installment plans are recorded as **Deferred Revenue**. * Recognise *Earned Revenue* each month proportionally to elapsed payment period. * This keeps the revenue curve smooth and prevents a spike on the month of sign‑up. 3. **Cost Allocation** * Region‑specific marketing spend is **cost‑allocated** to the units that generated those revenue streams. * Core platform cost is distributed based on **monthly active users (MAU)** per region. 4. **KPI Calculation** * **ARPU (USD)** = Total revenue (USD) / Total MAU. * **CAC** = Localized marketing spend (USD) / New users. * **LTV** = (ARPU × \(1 / churn\_rate\)) – (service costs per user). 5. **Defensible Benchmark** * We set a **minimum LTV/CAC ratio of 3** across all regions. If a market dips below, we re‑price and/or tighten acquisition spend. --- ## 8. Pricing Elasticity & Continuous Optimization | Tool | How it Works | Output | |------|--------------|--------| | **Dynamic Pricing Engine** | Uses real‑time sign‑up‑rate, churn, and regional GDP data. | Auto‑adjusts price in 5 % increments within permitted ranges. | | **A/B Test Matrix** | 10‑day runs on price + bundle (e.g., 6‑month vs 12‑month). | Determines elasticity curves for each market. | | **Churn Predictors** | Machine‑learning on device usage, streaming time, and payment behavior. | Identifies high‑churn subscribers; targeted retention offers. | | **Promotional Calendar** | Seasonal discounts synced with local holidays (e.g., Ramadan, Lunar New Year, Diwali, Black Friday). | Boosts ARPU during key windows without harming annualized revenue. | **Iteration Cycle:** - **Week 1–2:** Deploy new price set; monitor sign‑up, churn, ARPU. - **Week 3:** Adjust based on regression analysis. - **Month 3:** Formal KPI review; realign pricing if LTV < 3 × CAC. --- ## 9. Risk Management & Mitigation | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | |------|------------|--------|------------| | **Local Currency Depreciation** | Medium | Revenue erosion in USD terms | Hedge reserves in USD, price floor in local currency | | **Payment Regulation Changes** | Low‑Medium | Access to mobile‑money APIs affected | Local legal + regulatory monitoring, diversified payment partners | | **Family‑share Abuse** | Low | Revenue leakage, churn spikes | IP-based seat tracking, weekly usage audit | | **Ad‑Blockers** | Medium (African & Latin) | Loss of ad‑revenue | Offer higher‑quality, non‑intrusive ad units; push free‑premium tier | | **Data Privacy** | Medium | Regulatory fines, brand trust | Comply with GDPR, LGPD (Brazil). Use local data centers where required | --- ## 10. Implementation Roadmap | Phase | Timeframe | Deliverables | |-------|-----------|-------------| | **P0 – Market Discovery** | Month 0–1 | Country‑specific price‑elasticity models; partner‑network list (mobile‑money, BNPL). | | **P1 – Pricing Pilot** | Month 2–4 | Launch 3‑tier pricing + Family‑Bundle in 3 pilot countries (e.g., Kenya, India, Colombia). • Deploy A/B tests. | | **P2 – Scale & Optimize** | Month 5–8 | Rollout to 12 markets; refine dynamic pricing; automate currency conversion ledger. | | **P3 – Consolidation & Reporting** | Month 9–12 | Set up consolidated dashboard; integrate cost allocation; test unit‑economic thresholds. | | **P4 – Growth Loop** | Year 2 | Introduce “Pay‑As‑You‑Go” passes; expand into new emerging markets (UAE, Turkey, Mexico). | --- ## 11. Quick‑Reference Pricing Table (Approx. Values) | Country | Currency | Basic‑Ad | Standard | Premium | Family | |---------|----------|----------|----------|---------|--------| | Kenya (KES) | 400 | – | 280 | 425 | 650 | | Nigeria (NGN) | 1,200 | – | 900 | 1,400 | 2,200 | | India (INR) | 300 | 0 | 225 | 335 | 570 | | Bangladesh (BDT) | 200 | – | 150 | 225 | 380 | | Colombia (COP) | 8,000 | 1,000 | 5,500 | 7,750 | 12,000 | | Mexico (MXN) | 120 | 25 | 70 | 95 | 140 | | Brazil (BRL) | 10 | 3 | 7 | 10 | 15 | *All the above figure ranges are rounded to the nearest local currency unit and reflect the current USD‑PPP conversion (1 USD ≈ 350 NGN, 1 USD ≈ 75 INR, etc.). Prices can be tweaked ± 5 % without impacting consolidated ratios.* --- ## 12. Final Take‑away 1. **Localized price points** anchored by PPP and local currency purchase power keep *per‑user value* in check while giving local consumers a perceived fair deal. 2. **Flexible payment rails & families** match the true payment culture of each region, turning subscription sign‑ups into *reliable revenue streams*. 3. **Ad‑supported tiers** provide an additional revenue layer that offsets the lower price in low‑income markets, keeping unit economics stable. 4. A *dynamic, data‑driven pricing engine* protects the consolidated USD unit economics by continuously steering each region toward the target ARPU / LTV ratio. 5. All of this can be aggregated into a single consolidated financial view because every transaction is converted to USD on settlement, with deferred revenue properly accounted for. Implementing the above strategy will position the platform to scale profit‑ably through African, South‑Asian and Latin‑American markets while satisfying the expectations of both local subscribers and the investment community that looks for sharp, defensible unit economics.

run.userPrompt:
In 2026, a global streaming service is shifting from uniform USD pricing to localized subscription models. Purchasing power, preferred payment rails (mobile money, QR systems, installments), family-sharing norms, and attitudes toward recurring billing differ strongly across its African, South Asian, and Latin American growth markets, while headquarters still reports revenue in consolidated USD.

Propose a pricing and business-model strategy for localizing subscriptions across markets with different income levels, payment habits, and household-sharing norms, while keeping consolidated unit economics defensible to investors.
